parents.title: Welcome to the parent guide
parents.summary: What Leo Kids is, what parents can do on the site, and how to get started.

blocks.text: What is Leo Kids?
Leo Kids is a learning space for elementary learners in grades 1–6, with practice in math, geometry, English, and science, plus games and progress reports for parents.

blocks.alt: Leo Kids home page with learning and game areas
blocks.caption: Leo Kids home page with learning and game areas

blocks.text: The parent's role

items: Create a parent account and sign in
Add children and manage login details

parents.title: Create a parent account
parents.summary: How to sign up and enter the parent portal.

blocks.text: Login page
Go to the parent login page and complete sign-up or sign-in with your email and password.
Keep your login details in a safe place — you need them for every sign-in.

parents.title: Parent dashboard tour
parents.summary: Children list, adding a new child, and account limits.

blocks.text: Children list
On the parent page you will see all children linked to the account, with name, grade, and management options.
Account limits
By default, each parent account can include up to three children.
If you reach the limit, edit or remove an existing child before adding a new one.

parents.title: Add a child
parents.summary: Create a child profile, choose a grade, and save.

blocks.text: Add form
Enter the child's name and choose a grade (1 through 6). After saving, login details for the child will appear.

blocks.alt: Add child form with grade selection
blocks.caption: Add child form with grade selection

parents.title: PIN and login details for your child
parents.summary: What a PIN is, when it is shown once, and how to reset it.

blocks.text: What is a PIN?
Your child signs in with a username and a 4-digit code. After creation or reset, the code is shown once — save it.

blocks.alt: Message showing a new PIN code
blocks.caption: Message showing a new PIN code

blocks.text: Reset
On the parent page you can create a new login code for your child. The old code will stop working.
Do not share the code on social media or in public groups.

parents.title: Edit or delete a child
parents.summary: Change name or grade, and delete with confirmation.

blocks.text: Edit
Click edit next to the child's name, update details, and save.
Delete
Deletion requires typing the child's name to confirm — this cannot be undone.
Deleting a child removes their access and associated data from your account.

parents.title: How do I start reading the report?
parents.summary: A short introduction to the parent report and links to detailed guides.

blocks.text: Open a report
From the parent page, choose a child and click view report. You can switch between the standard and detailed report.

blocks.alt: Button to open a report from the parent page
blocks.caption: Button to open a report from the parent page

parents.title: Ask about the report (Copilot)
parents.summary: How to ask questions about the report and what the system can answer.

blocks.text: How to ask
Inside the report, open "Ask about the report" and type a question in English about performance, topics, or recommendations.
Limits

items: Answers are based on practice data on the site
They do not replace professional educational advice
Questions unrelated to the report may receive a general answer

parents.title: Monthly persistence reward
parents.summary: Persistence journey by subject and rewards for parents.

blocks.text: Persistence journey
Your child builds persistence through monthly practice. On the rewards page you can see progress by subject.

parents.title: Install as an app
parents.summary: Add Leo Kids to your phone or tablet home screen.

blocks.text: Install
On the home page or in the browser you may see "Install app" — tap and confirm. Then you can open Leo Kids like an app.
On iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen.

parents.title: Mobile and offline games
parents.summary: Using the site on a phone and playing without internet.

blocks.text: Using mobile
The site works on small screens. Student and parent login works from a phone too.
Offline
In the "Offline" area there are games that work on the same device without an internet connection.

parents.title: Login troubleshooting
parents.summary: Wrong PIN, locked account, and clearing browser cache.

blocks.text: Common issues

items: Wrong PIN — ask your parent for a new code
Page will not load — try refresh or clear browser cache

blocks.text: If the problem continues, contact us through the contact page.

parents.title: Privacy and data
parents.summary: What is collected during practice and how to reach us about privacy.

blocks.text: Practice data
The system stores practice data to show progress and reports. Do not share children's login codes with others.
For privacy questions or requests, see the privacy policy or contact us.

students.title: How do I sign in?
students.summary: Sign in with your username and PIN.

blocks.text: Steps

items: Ask your parent for your username and code
Type them on the login page

students.title: My home page
students.summary: What you see after signing in: subjects, coins, and avatar.

blocks.text: Home page
Here you will see your name, how many coins you have, and which subjects you can open.

blocks.alt: Student home page with subject cards
blocks.caption: Student home page with subject cards

students.title: Choose a subject and grade
students.summary: How to enter practice in the subject you picked.

blocks.text: Learning hub
Choose a subject from the list. Activities will match your grade.

blocks.alt: Subject list in the learning hub
blocks.caption: Subject list in the learning hub

blocks.text: Question types

items: Sometimes you choose an answer from a list
Sometimes you type a number or word
After your answer you will see if you were right

students.title: Hints and explanations
students.summary: What happens after a correct or incorrect answer.

blocks.text: After the answer
If you made a mistake — read the explanation and try again. If you were right — move to the next question!
Do not rush — reading the explanation helps you understand.

students.title: Daily missions
students.summary: Small tasks that help you move forward every day.

blocks.text: Missions
On your home page you will see daily missions. When you finish them, you earn points and progress.

students.title: Monthly persistence journey
students.summary: Practice each month and build progress.

blocks.text: Persistence
The more you practice in a month, the further your journey goes. It shows how much you kept going!

students.title: Coins and arcade
students.summary: How to earn coins and play online games.

blocks.text: Coins
Practice and earn coins. In the arcade you can play board-style games with friends.

students.title: Change your avatar
students.summary: How to choose a character or picture for your profile.

blocks.text: Avatar
Tap your picture on the home page and choose a new avatar.

students.title: Offline games
students.summary: Games without internet on the same device.

blocks.text: Offline
Tic-tac-toe and other games — no network needed.
Tips

items: Take a break if you are tired
Read explanations when you do not understand

blocks.text: Learning is more fun when you are not pressuring yourself!

parent-report.title: Parent report overview
parent-report.summary: Standard report vs detailed report — when to use each.

blocks.text: Standard report
Shows a quick picture: performance, trends, and main recommendations.
Detailed report
Includes breakdown by subject, topics, parent letter, and focused recommendations.

parent-report.title: Summary card
parent-report.summary: The top section of the report — overall picture.

blocks.text: Summary card
Briefly shows performance level, amount of practice, and the main message for what comes next.

blocks.alt: Summary card at the top of the report
blocks.caption: Summary card at the top of the report

parent-report.title: Enough data?
parent-report.summary: When a report has enough practice to show conclusions.

blocks.text: Data presence
If your child practiced only a little, the report will say there is not enough information yet. That is normal — keep practicing.
The more practice there is, the more accurate the report insights become.

parent-report.title: Trends and confidence level
parent-report.summary: How to read trend and confidence labels in the report.

blocks.text: Trends
A trend shows whether performance is improving, steady, or needs strengthening. Confidence level explains how reliable the data is.

parent-report.title: Strengths and areas to improve
parent-report.summary: What your child does well and what to strengthen.

blocks.text: Report sections

items: Strengths — topics where performance is strong
To improve — topics that need more practice

parent-report.title: Topics by subject
parent-report.summary: Breakdown by practice topics in each subject.

blocks.text: Topic tables
Each subject shows specific topics — for example addition in math or vocabulary in English.

parent-report.title: Overview of the four subjects
parent-report.summary: A chart or table comparing subjects.

blocks.text: Subjects chart
Lets you see at a glance where your child is strong and where there is room to grow across math, geometry, English, and science.

parent-report.title: Practice recommendations
parent-report.summary: What the system recommends to practice next.

blocks.text: Recommendations
Recommendations are based on repeating mistakes and topics not yet practiced enough.
Challenges
Challenges offer focused practice on topics that need strengthening.

parent-report.title: Detailed report
parent-report.summary: Executive summary, parent letter, and breakdown by subject.

blocks.text: Executive summary
General opening to the detailed report with the central message.
Parent letter
Each subject includes a written explanation for parents — what your child knows and what to strengthen.

parent-report.title: Print and PDF export
parent-report.summary: How to save or print the report.

blocks.text: Export
The report can be exported to PDF or printed — useful for a meeting with a teacher.
Before printing, check the preview to make sure everything fits on the page.

parent-report.title: Understanding the important notice
parent-report.summary: What the notice at the bottom of the report means — full text.

blocks.text: Important notice
Every report includes a notice explaining that the report is a support tool, not a professional diagnosis. Full text:

blocks.title: Important notice
paragraphs: The report is based on practice data collected on Leo Kids.
The report is meant to help parents understand what their child practiced, where strengths appeared, and what to strengthen next.

The report is not a medical, psychological, or educational diagnosis and does not replace a teacher, counselor, assessor, or other professional. If you have ongoing concerns about learning difficulty or gaps, speak with a teacher or qualified professional.

blocks.alt: Important notice box in a parent report
blocks.caption: Important notice box in a parent report

subjects.title: Math guide
subjects.summary: Math practice for grades 1–6 — what children learn and how to practice.

blocks.text: Who is it for?
Practice is designed for children in grades 1 through 6, matched to grade level.
What do we practice?
What does practice look like?
Choose a grade and level, answer questions, and get an explanation after each answer.
Tips
Practice at a steady pace — a little each day beats a lot on one day.
